Summary: Introductory partner discovery between Redwood and SolsticeGrid to explore a hybrid integration: SolsticeGrid wants a SaaS offering with optional on-prem GPU peering for regulated customers. Key concerns: data residency, private control plane, KMS integration, predictable latency, and pilot economics. Redwood AE+SE outlined hosted/dedicated/private options, smart routing and KV/prefix caching, and proposed a technical deep dive and benchmark as next steps.
Transcript:
Header: 2026-03-07 14:00 PT | Duration: 48m | Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam Ortega (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (SolsticeGrid CTO), Daniel Hughes (Lead SRE), Marcos Alvarez (Platform Engineer)

[00:00] Maya: hey everyone, thanks for joining on a Saturday — I appreciate it, I'll kick off. quick round robin?
[00:07] Priya: hi, Priya here. CTO, we run SolsticeGrid's SaaS platform and we are looking at a feature to let enterprise customers run certain workloads on their own racks but still hit our control plane.
[00:15] Daniel: daniel here, lead SRE. main ask is predictability — latency needs to be within a tight SLA for inferencing, plus we have strict network and audit constraints.
[00:22] Marcos: marcos, platform eng. i'll be building the peering and on-prem runtime.
[00:27] Maya: great, thanks. Liam, want to intro the technical part?
[00:31] Liam: yeah quick hi — i'm liam, infra SE. i'll cover runtime/latency and what's feasible. okay um, first question from our side: are you thinking a full private control plane on their network or VPC peering to our private endpoint?
[00:45] Priya: mostly V-P-C peering and optional air-gapped for very regulated customers. some customers will demand no outbound, so we need an on-prem package or an appliance.
[00:58] Maya: sounds similar to other partners. Redwood offers hosted API, dedicated reservation pools, and a private deploy — all the same API surface. you can pin model versions and route requests.
[01:10] Daniel: can you talk about KV cache and prefix caching? some of our workloads are prompt-heavy and we'd like to avoid repeat compute.
[01:18] Liam: yeah. we do prefix/K-V cache — sorry sometimes transcriber writes it as K-V cash — but the idea is we cache recurrent KV entries to avoid re-compute for repeated context. for cross-site, you'd either have a local cache on their on-prem runtime or route to regional caches.
[01:34] Marcos: and how does that interact with model variants/quantization?
[01:37] Liam: good question. we can run quantized variants (8-bit/4-bit) in the on-prem runtime. kernel selection and compilation adapts per hardware. so if they have A100-ish or H100, we pick different kernels; latency will differ.
[01:52] Priya: our ops lead is worried about key management — KMS. we cannot have customer keys leaving the customer's HSM. does Redwood support customer-managed KMS or HSM?
[02:03] Maya: yes, for Private deployments we support customer-managed K-M-S and H-S-M. for hosted, we offer encrypted-at-rest and customer BYOK integration via KMS proxies. i'll send the integration doc.
[02:18] Priya: are there SOC 2/ISO artifacts? auditors will ask.
[02:22] Maya: yes SOC2 Type II, ISO certs — we'll share those docs in the security bundle.
[02:27] Daniel: from a network perspective, we need a detailed diagram: what ports, how do you do mutual TLS and auth?
[02:33] Liam: we authenticate via mTLS for the private control plane; SAML/SSO for user auth. our peering options include IP allowlists, and we can provision private endpoints inside your VPC.
[02:44] Marcos: any notes on on-prem resource requirements? GPU configs?
[02:48] Liam: baseline: 1xA100-40GB equiv per small shard for medium throughput. for latency-critical workloads you'd want 2-4 GPUs per shard or a dedicated pool. for heavy batching workloads, more memory helps KV caching. we'll produce a perf matrix.
[03:05] Priya: can Redwood do smart routing between hosted and on-prem based on SLA? e.g., fall back to hosted if on-prem is saturated?
[03:13] Maya: yep. our smart routing can route by policy (latency/cost/region), and we can auto-fallback to compatible model variants in another region or hosted mode. usual caveat — model compatibility depends on quantization and architecture.
[03:27] Daniel: what about privacy — logs and audit? we need audit logs for all admin actions and token scoping.
[03:33] Maya: audit logs are part of the Private offering; we support token scoping and per-route RBAC. logs can be forwarded to your SIEM.
[03:41] Marcos: curious about cost model for hybrid: per-token hosted billing vs reserved dedicated on-prem license?
[03:48] Maya: we do usage-based for hosted, reserved capacity contracts for Dedicated, and enterprise licensing/extended support for Private. hybrid pilots often mix: reserved for on-prem fleet + host burst capacity. we'll send a sample pricing sheet.
[04:01] Priya: we'd like an estimate for a pilot: 10 enterprise customers each with 4-8 concurrent sessions, p95 latency target 250ms, primarily LLM chat inference.
[04:12] Liam: rough back-of-envelope: if it's chat with sequence lengths ~1k tokens and quantized models on A100-class, we can ballpark GPU needs; i'll quantify and put numbers in the follow-up.
[04:24] Maya: ok — logistics: are you open to a week-long bare-metal benchmark? we can run a small dataset to measure latency and tail behavior.
[04:32] Priya: yes, that's exactly what we want. 
[04:36] Daniel: schedule it after we share network/infra diagrams — need to ensure traffic routing is realistic.
[04:41] Marcos: one more thing: some of our customers need data residency in EU. can you pin model hosting to EU regions for those tenants?
[04:49] Maya: absolutely — routing by region and tenancy is supported. we can also ship on-prem packages for full EU-residency use cases.
[04:58] Priya: curious about latency hit when using quantized 4-bit vs full fp16 — do you have numbers?
[05:03] Liam: generally 4-bit can reduce memory and increase throughput but if you need strict latency at p95, sometimes fp16 on enough GPU cores is better. we'll include rough deltas in the perf matrix.
[05:15] Priya: any existing customers using hybrid on-prem peering?
[05:19] Maya: yes, a few enterprise customers in fintech and healthcare. one common pattern: private control plane with on-prem inference pods for regulated workloads and host for non-sensitive.
[05:30] Daniel: data plane encryption — is traffic end-to-end encrypted?
[05:33] Liam: yes, mTLS for control plane, and we encrypt data at rest with customer key options. we can also provide an air-gapped deployment if needed.
[05:43] Marcos: are there size constraints for the on-prem runtime container? we run limited namespaces.
[05:47] Liam: our on-prem runtime can run as a container or VM image; minimum disk ~120GB for model weights + cache, but it depends on model family and quantization. we'll add a sizing guide.
[05:58] [10:00 marker skipped — meeting continues, transcription with some overlap and mis-hearings]
[10:05] Maya: ok shifting to pilot success criteria — Priya, what would make this pilot a success for SolsticeGrid?
[10:12] Priya: motion to internalize: 1) p95 latency < 250ms for the sample workload 2) keys never leave customer H-S-M 3) audit logs flow to our Splunk 4) no more than 2x cost over baseline per request — sounds reasonable?
[10:28] Maya: yes, all reasonable. we'll aim to design around those.
[10:34] Daniel: about billing — can we have a billing API or metering exports?
[10:38] Maya: metering exports and token-level cost breakdowns are available; we can push to your billing bucket or S3.
[10:44] Marcos: any dev experience notes for app teams? SDKs?
[10:47] Maya: same SDKs across hosted/dedicated/private; function-calling, streaming, and structured output supported. no code changes for simple cases, just endpoint swap and creds.
[10:58] Priya: security review — we'll need a list of sub-processors and third-party vendors.
[11:03] Maya: sure, we'll include subcontractors and infra providers in the security pack.
[11:08] Daniel: are there rate limits or throttling on the private control plane?
[11:12] Liam: you can configure rate limits per-tenant; for private deployments control is mostly in your hands but defaults exist.
[11:19] Priya: do you support SSO via SAML/Okta?
[11:23] Maya: yes SAML/Okta and OIDC.
[11:27] Marcos: what about autoscaling policies for the on-prem fleet?
[11:31] Liam: autoscaling relies on cluster autoscaler or our node management; we can configure scale-out thresholds and burst capacity, though on-prem you'll be bounded by local capacity.
[11:40] [20:00 mark — more detailed noise and clarifications]
[20:07] Daniel: one concern — we'll have to route across a private fiber between SolsticeGrid data centers and customer racks. we need to test tail latency under real network flaps.
[20:16] Liam: that's exactly what a bare-metal benchmark gives you; we'll run induced packet loss and measure p99 tails.
[20:22] Priya: ok great. for the benchmark data set — can we use synthetic prompts and also a redacted real sample?
[20:30] Maya: yes, synthetic + redacted works. we'll provide a template.
[20:35] Daniel: timeline — can we do the benchmark mid-March?
[20:39] Maya: yes week of March 16 looks feasible.
[20:42] Marcos: about install — do you need privileged access to hardware?
[20:46] Liam: we'll need admin access to deploy runtime, or we can provide an installer that your SRE runs. for H-S-M integration we'll need to coordinate with your security team.
[20:56] Priya: another compliance question: how long do you retain logs by default?
[21:00] Maya: default retention is 90 days, configurable. for enterprise we can negotiate retention and export to your SIEM.
[21:06] Daniel: will you allow local-only model weights, not stored in Redwood control plane?
[21:11] Liam: yes — on-prem option can keep weights local. for hosted/dedicated we keep versioning in control plane, but for private we can decouple weight storage.
[21:23] Priya: are there any known limitations with model sizes >70B?
[21:27] Liam: large models will need more memory and multi-GPU tiling; performance varies and we'll call that out in the perf doc.
[21:34] Marcos: can we run a small A/B between quantized and fp16 in the benchmark?
[21:38] Maya: yes. we'll plan runs for fp16, 8-bit, and 4-bit if you want.
[21:44] [30:00 mark — wrap-up items and commitments]
[30:01] Maya: quick recap — next steps: security bundle, perf matrix, pilot pricing, schedule benchmark. anything else?
[30:08] Priya: add network diagram from our side.
[30:12] Daniel: and a clear list of ports and mTLS cert exchange steps.
[30:16] Marcos: i'd like a sizing guide for disk and cache too.
[30:20] Maya: noted. we'll follow up with a doc bundle and calendar invites.
[30:25] Priya: timeline: if we get those docs this week we can do the benchmark mid-March and decide by end of March.
[30:33] Maya: sounds good. I'll send the security pack and pricing by Friday.
[30:38] Liam: i'll own the perf matrix and benchmark plan.
[30:42] Maya: awesome, thanks everyone. closing now.
[30:45] Priya: thank you.
[30:47] Daniel: thanks, bye.
[30:48] Marcos: bye.
